EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces imminent escalation as Iran's new Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, issued a definitive vow of revenge for his assassinated father, Ali Khamenei, while the U.S. delivered a 24-hour ultimatum for Iran to publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open for shipping or face "serious consequences." This direct confrontation is exacerbated by a significant explosion near Iran's Parchin military complex and increasing U.S. pessimism regarding a nuclear deal without Iran surrendering enriched uranium.

IRAN
Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei has emerged as the new Supreme Leader, issuing a written statement on July 11, vowing "definite" revenge for his assassinated father, Ali Khamenei. He threatened that those responsible, "from the most senior to the most junior," would "take to their graves the dream of dying peacefully in their beds," emphasizing that this vengeance is a national demand and will occur regardless of his personal involvement. Mohammed Javad Khamenei, Ali Khamenei's eldest grandson, was identified as the masked figure at the funeral, reportedly suffering burns from the attack that killed his grandfather.

A major explosion occurred near the sensitive Parchin military complex in eastern Tehran on July 11, causing widespread shaking felt in Pakdasht, Qiamdasht, Qarčak, Khavar Shahr, Rey, and Pardis, with some residents reporting smoke. While the Pakdasht governor claimed it was a "controlled demolition of leftover ammunition," opposition sources suggested an attack. Satellite imagery observed by CNN revealed significant new activity at Parchin (Telagan 2) and Koh Kalan sites in late June and early July, including tunnel excavation and repair work, raising concerns about nuclear-related activities.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Muscat, Oman, for talks with Omani officials, joined by Qatari representatives. Iran maintains that the Strait falls exclusively within Iranian and Omani territorial waters, and any decisions on its management will be made by these two coastal states. An Iranian intelligence source reiterated Tehran's commitment to implementing the "Hormuz plan" despite U.S. threats and media pressure. Press TV reported that Iran's acting Defense Minister, Brig. Gen. Majid Ibn Reza, stated that drone production tripled during the recent US-Israeli war, and Iran's armed forces are closely monitoring enemy movements, knowing how and when to pressure the enemy. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeel Baqaee stated Iran would not permit inspections of facilities damaged by U.S. and Israeli attacks, asserting that UN Security Council Resolution 2231 is legally invalid. Fars News Agency, close to the IRGC, suggested striking Jebel Ali port in the UAE and Haifa port in Israel as a response to U.S. attacks on railway bridges, aiming to disrupt the IMEC corridor.

Internally, Iran reported the killing of two Basij volunteer forces, Seyed Sajjad Alavi and Mehdi Honarmand, during a security patrol for Ali Khamenei's funeral in Mashhad on July 11, initially described by a Khorasan Razavi security deputy as a "personal dispute." Widespread electricity outages, lasting several hours, affected various cities including Tehran, Mashhad, Tabriz, Urmia, and Karaj, following the funeral. The Prosecutor General announced over 300 indictments against individuals linked to "hostile media networks."

ISRAEL
The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) carried out targeted airstrikes in southern Lebanon on July 11, eliminating Hezbollah operatives. Forces of the 91st "Galilee" Regional Division identified Hezbollah operatives transporting anti-tank missiles in a vehicle into a building within Israel's south Lebanon buffer zone. An airstrike on the structure caused secondary explosions, indicating the presence of additional weapons. In a separate operation, the IDF killed a Hezbollah operative identified near a tunnel shaft at the Ali Taher ridge in the south Lebanon buffer zone and another suspect in a vehicle posing a threat to troops. Lebanese media reported multiple Israeli strikes in Mansouri.

On the home front, a 19-year-old was fatally stabbed in an Airbnb in Jerusalem's Nachlaot neighborhood, an incident described as criminal. Two young men sustained moderate injuries in a shooting in Umm al-Fahm. In Haifa, a man was moderately wounded in a stabbing on Andrea Sakharov Street, and two men in their 30s were severely injured in a separate stabbing near Student Beach, both criminal incidents. A 32-year-old man was critically injured in a shooting in Jaffa's Jerusalem Boulevard, also believed to be criminal. Protests against the government were noted in Nahalal and Haifa, and Haredi demonstrations in Jerusalem's HaNevi'im Street led to traffic disruptions and the arrest of a minor for assaulting a policewoman.

In the West Bank, U.S. Congressman Ro Khanna reported being detained by armed settlers during a visit, which he described as an "unfiltered look at the human cost of the Israeli occupation." Four suspects were arrested in Sinjil for damaging a foreign media vehicle, with clubs and a knife found in their car. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced plans to construct three new Israeli settlements in northern Gaza. Israel and India are in talks for the local production of Tamir interceptor missiles for the Iron Dome system.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The UN reported that Israel's demolition campaign in the occupied West Bank resulted in the displacement of dozens of Palestinians during the first ten days of July. Israeli forces conducted operations to extract a female Israeli soldier and her Palestinian partner from Jericho, as well as two other Israeli women who had entered the city to meet Palestinian acquaintances. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced intentions to develop three new Israeli settlements in the northern Gaza Strip.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operatives were observed transporting anti-tank missiles and other weapons into a building within Israel's south Lebanon buffer zone, prompting an Israeli airstrike that resulted in secondary explosions. An additional Hezbollah operative was killed near a tunnel shaft within the massive underground complex at Ali Taher ridge in the buffer zone, and another suspect in a vehicle deemed a threat was also neutralized by the IDF. Lebanese media, including Press TV, reported multiple Israeli airstrikes in the southern town of Mansouri, and additional Israeli drone strikes in Kfar Tebnit, with Israeli forces reportedly setting fire to Lebanese homes in Houla. Casualties from these strikes included at least one killed and several injured.

Diplomatic efforts are underway, with the French Press Agency reporting that the next round of Lebanon-Israel talks is scheduled for July 15-16 in Rome, hosted by Italy at the request of the U.S. Germany's Foreign Minister indicated that Berlin and Paris are jointly drafting a plan to address the situation in Lebanon. A Hezbollah lawmaker affirmed Iran's commitment to political and field support for Lebanon, linking an end to Israeli military offensives there with an end to the war against Iran. A U.S. military delegation met with Lebanese military commanders in Beirut to discuss a mechanism for implementing a "test zone" in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Israeli regime reportedly expanded its "invasion" into new areas of the Quneitra governorate in southwestern Syria. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported 15 Israeli ground incursions and attacks in parts of Dar'a and Quneitra over the past 10 days, involving approximately 30 military vehicles, with a focus on the Hauran Yarmouk basin and villages bordering the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights. Airstrikes, believed to be conducted by the International Coalition, targeted a cave in Jebel al-Dhahaak in Sokhna, Homs province. Explosions were also reported in Fo'a and Kafraya in Syria's Idlib province, attributed to targeting "terrorist factions of foreign nationalities."

In Iraq, explosions were heard in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, with reports indicating targets were "separatist opposition groups against Iran." The Iraqi Kata’ib Hezbollah chief reiterated the group's commitment to the resistance path and rejected enemy threats. The "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" issued a statement vowing to qualitatively and quantitatively develop its military and security capabilities in response to what it termed "U.S.-Zionist threats." Iraqi security forces were deployed around the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra amid rising tensions and protests following the killing of an Iraqi fisherman, Najem Abdullah, by Kuwaiti coast guard personnel. The Iraqi Prime Minister instructed the Foreign Ministry and Army Chief of Staff to investigate the incident. Iraq's National Security Advisor, Qasim al-Araji, emphasized that Gulf security is a shared regional interest and a collective responsibility. There were reports of fires at railway warehouses in central Baghdad and near Baghdad International Airport (Dublin base), and an armed attack on a mourning council in Sadr City. Denis Citrinovitch, former head of the Iran desk for Israeli military intelligence, dismissed claims that Iran is losing influence in Iraq as "wishful thinking," asserting that Baghdad remains a "first-rate strategic asset" for Tehran.

GULF STATES
The Strait of Hormuz remained a critical point of contention. Oman hosted Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi for talks on bilateral relations, regional developments, and the administration of the Strait, specifically referring to Article 5 of the Islamabad MoU. Qatar participated in these discussions, acting in a mediating role and facilitating an exchange of views, although Iran clarified that Qatar holds no influence over decisions regarding the Strait.

The U.S. issued a demand for Iran to publicly declare by Saturday, July 11, that the Strait of Hormuz is open for shipping and that it will cease attacks on commercial vessels, warning of "serious consequences" if Tehran fails to comply. This comes amidst claims from U.S. officials that Iran had privately admitted to "mistakenly" shooting at commercial ships, attributing these actions to "rogue" hardline elements or a "technical fault." An Iranian intelligence source, however, stated that Iran would proceed with its Hormuz administration plans despite U.S. threats and media pressure. A Chinese shipping company was reported to be moving at an extremely slow pace in the Strait, with speculation suggesting it may have been attacked by Iran for using an "American corridor."

U.S. President Donald Trump held a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Tensions between Iraq and Kuwait escalated following the killing of an Iraqi fisherman by Kuwaiti coast guard personnel, leading to Iraqi military deployments around the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra. The U.S. Justice Department ordered New York Times journalists to testify before a federal grand jury concerning their reporting on security concerns related to a new Air Force One aircraft donated by Qatar. China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports, effective immediately, citing the escalating tensions in West Asia and the need to secure supplies for its domestic chip manufacturing industry.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Mujtaba Khamenei's Revenge Vow:** Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, the new Supreme Leader of Iran, issued a written statement on July 11, vowing "definite" revenge for his assassinated father, Ali Khamenei, and threatening those responsible.
2.  **U.S. Ultimatum on Strait of Hormuz:** The U.S. demanded Iran publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open for shipping and commit to halting attacks on vessels by Saturday, July 11, warning of "serious consequences" otherwise.
3.  **Tehran Explosion & Nuclear Site Activity:** A significant explosion occurred near Iran's sensitive Parchin military complex in eastern Tehran on July 11. While officially attributed to controlled demolition, CNN satellite images reveal recent construction and repair activities at Parchin and other Iranian nuclear/military sites.
4.  **Israeli Strikes in Southern Lebanon:** The IDF conducted multiple airstrikes in southern Lebanon on July 11, targeting Hezbollah operatives transporting weapons and an operative near a tunnel shaft at Ali Taher ridge, causing secondary explosions and resulting in at least one fatality.
5.  **U.S. Pessimism on Iran Nuclear Deal:** U.S. officials expressed growing pessimism about reaching a nuclear deal with Iran, stating that no agreement is possible without Iran relinquishing its enriched uranium.
6.  **Israeli Incursions into Syria:** The Israeli regime reportedly expanded its "invasion" into new areas of the Quneitra governorate and conducted 15 ground incursions/attacks in Dar'a and Quneitra in the past 10 days.
7.  **China's Helium Export Ban:** China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports, effective July 11, citing escalated tensions in West Asia and the need to secure domestic chip production.
8.  **Internal Casualties & Power Outages in Iran:** Two Basij forces were killed in Mashhad during a security patrol for Ali Khamenei's funeral on July 11, and widespread, multi-hour electricity outages were reported across several major Iranian cities.
9.  **Iraqi Resistance Threatens Escalation:** The "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" issued a statement on July 11, pledging to enhance military and security capabilities in response to what they described as "U.S.-Zionist threats."

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of widespread regional escalation is critically high, driven by the explicit revenge vow from Iran's new Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, directly confronting U.S. President Donald Trump's retaliatory threats of "complete decimation" of Iran. The Strait of Hormuz is an immediate flashpoint, with the U.S. imposing a Saturday, July 11 deadline for Iran to publicly commit to open navigation, backed by threats of "serious consequences." Concerns about Iran's nuclear program are escalating, with U.S. officials expressing deep pessimism about a deal without Iran's uranium surrender, compounded by satellite imagery suggesting renewed activity at sensitive Iranian military and nuclear sites like Parchin. Ongoing Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and into Syrian territory risk broadening the conflict. Iran's Fars News Agency's suggestion of striking Jebel Ali port (UAE) and Haifa port (Israel) indicates a potential for targeting critical infrastructure beyond direct military engagements, threatening regional economic stability and the IMEC corridor. The reported cooling system failure of the USS Boxer earlier in the conflict highlights vulnerabilities for U.S. assets. The volatile situation in Iraq, with Iraqi resistance groups pledging to expand capabilities against "U.S.-Zionist threats," indicates potential for proxy escalation.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The U.S. posture towards Iran is highly aggressive, with President Donald Trump threatening "1,000 missiles... aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran" and "complete decimation" for a year if any attempt is made on his life. The U.S. issued a 24-hour ultimatum, expiring on July 11, for Iran to publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open and cease attacks on commercial vessels, warning of "serious consequences." U.S. officials expressed diminishing optimism for a nuclear deal, stressing that a key condition is Iran's handover of enriched uranium. Trump also conversed with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The U.S. Justice Department controversially ordered New York Times journalists to testify before a federal grand jury concerning reports on security issues with a new Air Force One donated by Qatar.

Oman is playing a mediating role, hosting talks between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani officials regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with Qatar also participating in these discussions. Germany and France are reportedly drafting a joint plan for Lebanon, with Germany's Foreign Minister emphasizing diplomatic solutions over battlefield outcomes for both the Iran and Ukraine crises. Russia's Kremlin spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, warned of potential nuclear weapon use if the existence of the Russian state were threatened, while its Foreign Ministry criticized Ukraine's air defense issues amidst reports of Russian missile strikes on a Ukrainian oil depot. China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports due to escalating West Asia tensions, and President Xi Jinping reaffirmed traditional friendship with North Korea. Iraq's Prime Minister directed ministerial and military bodies to address the killing of an Iraqi fisherman by Kuwaiti coast guard, while Iraqi security forces deployed around the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra amidst rising tensions. India is engaging in military cooperation with Israel for the co-production of Iron Dome interceptor missiles.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant discrepancies exist in reporting on the attendance at Ali Khamenei's funeral; Iranian state media (Press TV, Fars News) claimed "tens of millions" or "more than 43 million" mourners, while another source (Kian Meli 1) cited international reports of 140,000 participants, 95% of whom were reportedly from outside Iran. This stark difference indicates a strong propaganda effort by Iranian state media to inflate public support.

The initial identity of the masked individual at Ali Khamenei's funeral was contradictory, with early reports (N12) suggesting Mojtaba Khamenei, later clarified (N12, Yediotnews25) to be Mohammed Javad Khamenei, the grandson, who reportedly sustained burns. Doubts about Mojtaba Khamenei's public presence persist, with claims (Omid Dana) that a recently released image of him is AI-generated, suggesting potential deliberate obfuscation or concerns about his true condition/status.

The explanation for the large explosion near the Parchin military complex on July 11 is highly contentious. While Iranian authorities (Pakdasht governor) attributed it to a "controlled demolition of leftover ammunition," eyewitness accounts described a massive blast and widespread shaking. This official narrative is further challenged by recent CNN satellite imagery showing repair and construction activity at Parchin, raising questions about the true nature of the incident.

U.S. officials' claims (WSJ, CBS News, Politico, Reuters) that Iran privately admitted "mistakes" in attacking commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, attributing them to "rogue" elements or "technical faults," are unverified by any public Iranian statement and could be a U.S. diplomatic tactic to pressure Tehran into a public concession.

The killing of two Basij forces in Mashhad during Ali Khamenei's funeral was initially downplayed by a local security deputy as a "personal dispute," only for the IRGC's local branch to later describe it as a "terrorist act." This inconsistency suggests an initial attempt to suppress or control information regarding security incidents during a high-profile national event.

An unverified and inflammatory claim (Omid Dana) suggests that student exams in Iran will be held near military bases, implying their use as human shields. This claim lacks corroboration and should be treated with extreme caution as a potential piece of disinformation.

A lack of specific details regarding the "Chinese shipping company stuck in Hormuz" and the claim of an "Iranian attack for using 'US corridor'" makes this unverified and potentially speculative.
